name: Accordion
summary: Stacked sections that open and close. Each title is a heading holding the system Button that toggles its section. One or many open at a time.
useWhen: A long page of settings or answers where people need one or two sections at a time, such as an FAQ or account settings
A side panel that groups many controls into named sections that can be folded away
Content that is useful but secondary, where a short title says enough to decide whether to open it
avoidWhen: Content that most people need: hiding it costs a click for everyone
Switching between views of the same thing, where only one shows at a time and the choice should stay visible
Steps that must be done in order
A single section that shows or hides one detail

type.description: single: one section open at a time. multiple: any number open.

collapsible.description: With type single: the open section can be closed again, so all can be closed.

value.description: The open section, controlled: a string with type single (empty closes all), a list of strings with type multiple. Pair with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: The section open at first: a string with type single, a list of strings with type multiple.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new value when a section opens or closes.

size.description: Trigger height and text size: sm is size.control.md (32px) with text s, md is size.control.lg (44px) with text m.

variant.description: data-variant. plain: no lines. divided: a border.default line under each section. card: each section on surface 2 with radius.panel and a gap.

headingLevel.description: The heading level, 2 to 6, that holds each trigger, so the sections fit the page outline.

disabled.description: On the root or an AccordionItem: the section cannot open or close. Its trigger keeps focus with aria-disabled and dims with opacity.disabled.

children.description: AccordionItem elements, each with one AccordionTrigger and one AccordionContent.

a11y.role: Each trigger is a native button with aria-expanded, and aria-controls while its section is open (Radix drops it when closed, which the APG pattern allows), inside a heading (level from headingLevel). Each open content is a region named by its trigger.
a11y.focus: Every trigger is in the tab order, disabled ones included (aria-disabled). The content's own controls follow their trigger. The trigger takes the Button's 2px focus ring.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next trigger, or into the open content
keys.Enter: Opens or closes the focused section
keys.Space: Opens or closes the focused section
keys.ArrowDown: Moves focus to the next trigger, from the last to the first
keys.ArrowUp: Moves focus to the previous trigger, from the first to the last
keys.Home: Moves focus to the first trigger
keys.End: Moves focus to the last trigger

a11y.announce: The trigger is announced as a button with its title and expanded or collapsed. The heading level lets screen reader users jump between sections.
notes: The order proposed an icon part. The trigger is the system Button, and a part inside it belongs to the Button, so the chevron is the Button's end content (data-part end), not an accordion part.
The chevron is the trigger Button's end content and is hidden from assistive tech; aria-expanded carries the state, the turn of the chevron shows it.
Arrow keys move up and down in both directions of text, as the sections stack.
Closed content is not in the page, so a search in the page does not find it.
Forced colors: the dividers and card edges become CanvasText lines; the trigger uses the Button's forced colors focus.
data-orientation is stamped by Radix on the root, items, headers and triggers, and is always vertical.

en.trigger: A noun that names the section, sentence case: Billing, Notifications. No question marks unless it is an FAQ.
en.content: Plain sentences. Say what the person can do here.

ar.trigger: Noun form, no diacritics: الفوترة، التنبيهات.

react.behavior: radix:Accordion, the trigger on the system Button through asChild
react.note: accordion-height: the content fades in and slides down space.xs as it opens (transform and opacity, duration.medium, ease.out), the chevron turns (transform). Closing is at once. Under reduced motion both are off.

angular.note: CDK accordion (cdkAccordion, cdkAccordionItem) with button[dsButton] as the trigger. Accordion.css as is.

native.note: rn-primitives accordion; the trigger is the native Button.

styles.studio: Ghost triggers on the page, a border.default line between sections in divided, surface 2 cards in card. The trigger hover is the 5% overlay.
styles.desk: The same, on Desk's surfaces and type. No recipe.
styles.liquid: Planned: card sections stay solid content.

mistakes.wrong: Putting a button or a link inside the trigger
mistakes.right: Keep the trigger to its title; put actions in the content

mistakes.wrong: Tabs drawn as an accordion to switch views
Every heading at level 3 inside a section that is already level 3
mistakes.right: Set headingLevel one below the heading that holds the accordion

mistakes.wrong: Hiding the one setting most people need inside a closed section
mistakes.right: Leave it open with defaultValue, or outside the accordion
